..
As of 245 AM EDT...

KEY MESSAGE 1... 

High pressure will be near eastern NY and western New England to
start the day and then will shift eastward to the Gulf of Maine
by late this afternoon and this evening. Some patchy radiative 
mist/fog in the major and sheltered valleys will burn off 
quickly after sunrise today with a cool start with lows in the 
40s to 50s. Expect max temps to be near normal today with still 
shallow mixing heights. We went close to a MAV/NBM blend with 
highs 80-85F in the valleys and 70s over the hills and mtns 
with a few upper 60s over the high peaks. Mostly clear skies and
light to calm winds will support radiative cooling once again, 
and we went below the NBM mins for Sunday morning with lows in 
the 50s with some upper 40s over the higher terrain. Patchy 
radiational mist/fog will be possible once again for the Glens 
Falls/Lake George Region, portions of the Upper and mid Hudson 
Valley and east of the southern Greens towards the CT River 
Valley. The 2nd half of the weekend will feature a slight 
moderation and warming trend in temps, as a weak sfc anticylone 
remains in control from near Nova Scotia southwest to the Ohio 
Valley, though weak mid and upper level ridging sets up aloft. 
An isolated pop-up shower or t-storm is possible near the 
west/south Dacks. Otherwise, dewpoints will be mainly in the 
50s in the valleys which will be quite comfortable. Highs temps 
will be near normal in the lower to mid 80s in the valleys/hills
and 70s to around 80F over the higher terrain which is 
climatologically normal for late July (i.e. normal high for 
Albany is 84F currently). Unsettled weather looks to return to 
start the week.


KEY MESSAGE 2...

A mid and upper level trough set up over the Northeast on 
Monday. Some mid and high clouds increase, as a short-wave moves
towards and across the region in the northwest flow aloft. The 
instability looks modest with weak shear on Monday based on 
some of the medium range and ensemble guidance. The showers and 
widely scattered t-storms may be most numerous over the the 
higher terrain and from the Capital District north and east. Max
temps continue to look seasonable with a slight uptick in 
humidity levels with dewpoints in the upper 50s to mid 60s.

Monday night into the midweek, the forecast becomes increasingly
more unsettled with the mid and upper level trough over NY and
New England. The guidance varies where a more potent short-wave
moves through the trough and impacts the region by Tue-Tue
night. A more recent trend with the majority of the medium range
guidance and ensembles is for a wave to develop to the south of
the forecast area and brings periods of showers/rain and few
thunderstorms Tue-Tue night with residual showers with the sfc
wave and upper low thru Wed. However, the ECMWF and some of the
ensembles have a 990-995 hPa low over west-central NY by Tue pm
closing off with periods of showers and thunderstorms. Some 
could be on the stronger side if enough instability sets up, but
the shear is not to impressive. PWATS do surge to about 1.50" 
with good moisture advection on Tue, and the latest NAEFS 
continues to show low and mid level height fall  2-3 STDEVs 
below normal. NBM 24-hr probabilities >1" of rainfall are 45-60%
across all of eastern NY and western New England by 12Z/Wed 
with some additional rainfall thereafter. PWAT anomalies form 
the latest NAEFS are 1-2 STDEVs above normal. WPC guidance 
supports about 1-2.5" of rainfall for Tue thru Wed and the 
Excessive Rainfall Outlook has the entire area in a 'Marginal 
Risk' for Tue-Tue night. Antecedent soil conditions are dry (not
much rainfall the past 5-days) leading into the event with high
gridded FFG values. However, any training cells or bands could 
lead to ponding of water on roads, urban and poor drainage
nuisance flooding or an isolated instance of a flash flood. 
This event could be a widespread, beneficial soaking rainfall 
too. We will continue to monitor potential impacts over the next
few days. 

Temps trend cooler than normal Tue-Thu with the mid and upper 
closed/cut-off low and associated clouds and rain-cooler air. 
The showers begin to decrease and become isolated to scattered 
by Thu...with fair weather and more seasonable temps to close 
the week.
